objective: Execute the authoritative projectSlice contract against the frozen GameSpec: prove and repair one player-complete Godot graybox, approve coherent whole-scene targets, then integrate one visually production-ready encounter with state-linked motion and artifact-backed evidence. Use a separate tournament campaign only for a named unresolved fork. Do not present graybox, concept, generated source, extracted source, or engine-ready assets as production.

nodes.instructions: Perform a fail-closed recovery preflight over the SHA-verified slice-v6 source imported into this candidate. Read design/recovery/slice-v6-preserved-import.json, the approved scene target, its validation manifest, production inventory and reports, design system, and game/main.gd. Verify scene-target.json and validation.json bind the identical approved status, reviewer, selected target id, selected primary-view hash, and approvedAt; repair only approval metadata if inconsistent. Validate every declared source and runtime component hash that can be recomputed. Run Godot import plus the clean-start and returning-player deterministic scenarios against the recovered source. Do not reopen the visual direction, regenerate targets or assets, or claim stale candidate evidence as current. Remove or replace stale evidence and record exact remaining gaps for downstream refresh. On a repair invocation, consume the reviewer findings and make the smallest bounded correction.

Review the recovered full-scene targets at the shipping camera before component production resumes. Verify actual gameplay, interaction hierarchy, required states, text zones, relative scale, navigation, and engine feasibility from design/scene-targets/scene-target.json, validation.json, the rendered views, and the current Godot implementation. Audit declared peer regions, typography, and the restrained motion plan. Reject concept art, nonsensical controls, frozen tableaux, decorative clutter, inconsistent scale, or a target that cannot be decomposed. Do not regenerate or revise target files in this recovery gate. On pass, the structured result MUST use this exact shape at minimum: {"outcome":"pass","summary":"...","findings":{"selectedTargetId":"...","selectedTargetSha256":"64 lowercase hex characters"}}. Do not nest selectedTargetId or selectedTargetSha256 under approval or another object. Return revise with prioritized scene-level changes if the recovered target no longer passes.

Record the passed scene-target-gate decision without changing its creative work. Read the gate's selected target id, selected primary-view hash, and findings. Atomically bind the decision into both design/scene-targets/scene-target.json and design/scene-targets/validation.json. In scene-target.json update only approval: status approved, reviewer scene-target-gate, selectedTargetSha256 equal to the gate-approved primary-view hash, findings copied from the review, and approvedAt as the current ISO timestamp. In validation.json mirror status, reviewer, selectedTargetId, selectedTargetSha256, and the identical approvedAt without changing measured checks. Validate scene-target.json as gamefactory.scene-target/v1 and fail if either manifest disagrees with the gate, selected view, or each other. Do not alter candidates, prompts, geometry, component maps, hashes, assets, or non-approval validation results.

Choose the smallest production method that can faithfully realize the approved scene target. Preserve creative latitude: return exactly one outcome from direct, segment, motion_study, pixel_motion, or segment_pixel_motion. Use direct for code-native work or assets that need neither segmentation nor generated motion. Use segment only when approved whole-scene imagery should be decomposed with SAM 3. Use motion_study only when an external generated video is useful as non-runtime motion reference. Use pixel_motion when a generated motion study should be tracked and compiled into palette-locked runtime frames; add segmentation only when static scene components also need extraction. Before selecting a provider lane, verify its configured request path and prerequisites are available; never select a paid or credentialed provider merely because it exists. Write design/asset-lanes/decision.json with rationale, selected outcome, required components, source scene ids and hashes, and expected outputs. For every selected lane, also write its valid candidate-local request: sam3.request.json, video.request.json, sam3.video.request.json, and/or pixel-motion.request.json. Pin the approved scene images as references and choose contained output directories. Do not generate or integrate assets in this node.

Recovery continuation: read design/recovery/runtime-bootstrap.json before doing anything else. The recovered game logic and licensed fonts are valid, but fourteen lost slice-v6 rasters are explicitly compile-only bootstraps and MUST NOT survive production acceptance. Re-author or target-link every mismatched raster from the approved whole-screen scene system, using SAM 3 or another configured lane when it materially improves coherent extraction; do not replace them with procedural geometry or transparent shims. Update the production inventory and integration provenance to the actual accepted files, mark the bootstrap superseded, and preserve the target's native geometry, peer-region ownership, typography roles, component footprints, runtime consumers, and state-linked motion. Then regenerate current real-engine first-session and returning-player scenarios, shipping-camera stills, representative motion recordings, capture index, integration report, motion report, polish report, and production-readiness hashes. Repair runtime code only when current engine evidence demonstrates a concrete mismatch. Treat any bootstrap asset, undeclared collision, clipping, stale evidence, missing consumer, hash drift, static actor, generic fallback, or absent causal motion as a blocker. Return every runtime source file named by the accepted production inventory—including rasters, fonts, license, and game/main.gd—as a structured artifact in addition to the manifests and current evidence, so a rejected candidate remains recoverable. Do not substitute a different visual direction or inherit the discarded candidate's captures as current evidence. If any required surface remains provisional, report visual-prototype rather than overstating maturity.

Inspect the current engine stills and motion recording, design-system hashes, polish manifest, runtime asset imports, interface-kit inventory and states, pixel-grid compliance, and both deterministic scenarios. Read design/recovery/runtime-bootstrap.json and return revise if it is not explicitly superseded, if any compile-only raster remains, or if any accepted production-inventory output is absent from the production-slice-builder's structured artifact list. Recompute runtime hashes from files rather than trusting candidate-authored manifest values. Verify that motion evidence comes from the running engine, includes moving actors and state-linked feedback, and covers action causality rather than a reconstructed promo or changing text over a static plate. Return pass only when evidence is current, complete, preserved, and internally consistent; otherwise return revise with exact stale, missing, unpreserved, or overstated claims.

Compare every production component and the current Godot capture against the approved whole-scene target and its state variants. Verify target-hash lineage, source view and crop, silhouette, material, palette, border density, typography relationship, ornament scale, native and render dimensions, and state consistency. Composite isolated components back into their approved target regions where useful. Reject unconditioned individual generations, assets derived from another target, style drift, approximate matches that change hierarchy, or a locally attractive component that weakens the complete screen. Return pass only when the assembled runtime recovers the approved scene language while remaining clear and engine-native; otherwise return revise with exact component and integration mismatches.

Judge the actual shipping-camera Godot stills and motion recording as a unified game experience. Inspect interface chrome as first-class art: panels, controls, meters, icons, states, feedback, and results must share one authored system. Audit the full viewport and every required state for accidental overlaps, clipping, competing layers, weak hierarchy, arbitrary stretching, mismatched density, and generic procedural fallback. Audit typography by role; reject tiny or ubiquitous pixel type that damages sustained reading or collapses hierarchy, while allowing intentional pixel, hybrid, or non-pixel systems. Inspect motion for controlled life as well as causality: ambient continuity, interaction response, gameplay consequence, defeat or resolution when relevant, and state transitions must feel coherent rather than frozen or filled with unrelated loops. Return pass only when the representative encounter looks intentionally authored and production-ready. Score focal_hierarchy, gameplay_legibility, layout_integrity, typography_coherence, interface_coherence, authored_specificity, target_fidelity, motion_feedback, and scene_life from 0-100, citing every required view and the current engine sequence. Never call the game fun without human evidence.

Make the final production-slice decision from the authoritative projectSlice contract, approved whole-scene target, scene review, current engine capture, component-fidelity findings, gameplay evidence, art-director findings, asset maturity, and polish manifest. Return pass only if every required surface is production, every required gate is evidenced, every runtime component is traceable to the selected scene target, and no blocker or runtime placeholder remains. On pass, include projectEvidence in the structured output: each required scenario as {id, artifactSha256}, interactionTrace, engineCapture, targetSha256, motionEvidence, and each required runtime asset as {id, consumer, artifactSha256}; every hash must identify an actual declared preserved artifact. Return revise rather than accepting a halfway state. If runtime evidence falsifies a consumed frozen claim rather than the implementation, return a projectDisposition of kind spec-amendment with rationale, consumed claimIds, and evidenceArtifactSha256; do not use that route for ordinary repairable defects.
